description: The team was founded by Rafael Andrade and Moacyr Pereira, two developers passionate about technology, innovation, and space programs. Our purpose is to combine knowledge, share ideas, and collaborate on developing creative and innovative technological solutions that can make a difference. We believe in the power of collaboration and technology to turn great ideas into impactful solutions.
summary:
The ARES Visor Simulator is a web-based, first-person simulator of Martian extravehicular activities (EVA), allowing users to explore Gale Crater, from Ares-1 Base to the boxwork formations of Mount Sharp. The environment was reconstructed using images and data from previous NASA missions, providing an immersive and realistic representation of the Martian landscape.

Guided by DUNA, an artificial intelligence agent, the system transforms data from 10 NASA sources into a navigation and survival guide. Using 1-meter HiRISE elevation data, it calculates safe routes, avoids slopes exceeding 25°, and monitors weather conditions (REMS), radiation levels (RAD), and solar storms (DONKI) before authorizing a mission.

Its key differentiator is its consideration of human physical limitations, prioritizing astronaut safety rather than simply finding the shortest route. The project addresses the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge by transforming real scientific data into an interactive exploration and decision-support experience for human survival on Mars.
details:
ARES Visor works through an interactive 3D simulation developed with Three.js and JavaScript, allowing users to explore Mars in first person, as if they were wearing a spacesuit helmet visor. The environment was built using images and information from previous missions, integrated with official NASA APIs and processed using Python-based tools.

Powered by Claude AI, DUNA acts as an exploration assistant, interpreting mission data and guiding the astronaut throughout the journey. Through Web Speech and Azure Speech, it enables voice interaction, making the experience more natural and immersive. API key security is managed through SoftwareBox Secrets.

The project's creativity lies in transforming real scientific data into an experience where users do not simply observe Mars, but must make decisions while considering the risks and physical limitations of a human explorer.

Beyond its potential to evolve into an immersive astronaut training tool and support mission planning, our goal is to bring Mars closer to everyone. The experience encourages curiosity and learning through voice and text features that promote accessibility for people with visual and hearing impairments, autistic individuals, older adults, and diverse audiences. We believe space exploration should also be an opportunity for inclusion, education, and bringing society closer to science.
